name: Shuffle-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The whole word is settled and readable, evenly spaced across the frame.

tagline: Wide letters roll into place one after another.
summary: The letters of a single word are split into vertical strips and rolled upward into their final shapes, so the word clicks into place a character at a time. Hovering replays the roll.
appearance: The word "SHUFFLE" runs across a black stage in wide-tracked, thin white capitals. Letterforms are simple and evenly spaced with plenty of air around them.
behaviour: On entering view each letter rolls vertically through a stack of copies before landing on the real glyph, staggered so the word assembles left to right. Hovering the word runs the roll again.
search_phrases: letters roll into place one by one
use_when: A single display word should arrive with a mechanical roll when seen or hovered.
avoid_when: Long lines or body text: the per-letter roll needs a short word to read.
customise: The text, tag, direction, duration, easing, stagger, roll count, hover trigger, loop and colour range are props.
weight_why: One short timeline on per-character strips; idle once it settles.

a11y.note: Replay is hover-only, so keyboard users cannot retrigger it; reduced motion is respected.

issues: Mid-roll frames show chopped glyph fragments that read as broken type out of context.
polish_why: Crisp wide tracking and a tidy roll; the split frames can look like broken type.
title: Shuffle
